With Iskandar permitting the creation and production of the magical circuit elements, Phaedrus' work could finally begin.

The careful application of moonfire right as the wafers were struck allowed the circuitry to be integrated into the disks. With sufficient production, experimentation could now begin.

Phaedrus considered all of the chips, the one with the most obvious weaponization potential was the one that applied a force directly away from its face. It was a simple chip design, with a simple function. The first temptation was to arrange the elements in a row, and feed magic in through one end. However, that led to an interesting observation. The magic drain was almost unchanged, and each module only emitted a small force, much less than they did individually.

An interesting result, Phaedrus saw that all of these were wired up in a sequence, and it decreased the power avaliable to each chip. Interesting. Was there another way to hook up the elements?

Phaedrus took one copper wire, and carefully arranged it so that all the "in" terminals of the wafers were connected to one side of the wire, then a bend, then all the "out" terminals were connected to the other. Then, magic was allowed to flow.

In a single instant, Phaedrus found himself blown across the room and harshly thrown against a wall, and the copper wire melted under the intense power that flowed through it. Interesting configuration, with interesting consequences.

Phaedrus pryed himself out of the wall, and shrugged away the pain. Apparantly, connecting the elements parallel to one another led to increased draw. Getting tossed back that hard was definitely promissing though, maybe this could be weaponized fairly quickly...

Maybe, with testing of different wires, this system could be made to not melt itself upon use.

*****

There, using some wood and test-tube holders, a container for the circuit was quickly made. This time, the connecting wires were made of silver, and substantially thicker. Some of the chips were placed in front of one another, to see if the effect could be made to accurately displace a block of spruce placed roughly 3.1415 m away.

Phaedrus closed a switch and let the magic flow into the circuit, in an instance, half of the wafers came out of their housing and were propelled at the spruce block, which was also knocked off of its pedistal. The rest of the apparatus flew backwards and shattered against the back wall of his office.

Phaedrus sighed, there was a lot of work ahead of him.

*****

Some more experiments with this parallel design showed that each element was outputting the exact same energy that the individual element had produced. This observation was interesting, and led to a thought. If the magic flowed, could it temporarily be stopped, left to build, and then released like a flood into a single element?

Phaedrus quickly set to work. None of the current element designs were designed for this purpose. It hadn't even been conceived until now, but he knew there had to be a way. The spectra inately had the ability to store a small quantity of this power, but it could not be held, and never for long. Yet there must be something that is being done by the vine, a sort of path, a pattern that could be replicated. Taking inspiration, Phaedrus visited the Hall of Force to witness the Order's solders train in the use of magic. A few things were recurrent. During the casting of particularly powerful spells, a particular vine pattern was always formed, leading the magic in the air around it to take a certain shape. The form was relatively simple, a set of parallel, but disconnected magical pathways.

Upon taking these observations, and making a few sketches of the circuit paths, he went and decided to create a new array design. Hopefully it would succeed, but for now, all Phaedrus could do was wait.

Phaedrus frowned, he absolutely detested waiting.

Phaedrus, having received the magical circuit elements, begins to experiment with force producing components. He takes the chip best described as a force circuit and tries to build a weapon out of it, only to shoot half the apparatus across the room. He then drafts up designs for a temporary power storage device and asked for the production of those elements.
